body:
Fixes #364 (in part — see **Scope**). Remaining data loss: #403.

`removeJunction` deleted `junction.wireIds.slice(1)`, treating index 0 as the trunk. That array is bookkeeping order, not structure, so on a **branch-first** junction it deleted the user's trunk and kept a branch. The feed wire is now found by structure, using the same `findJunctionFeedWire` the evaluator uses (#365) — one definition, so the store and the evaluator cannot disagree about a document.

## Scope — what this fixes, and what it does not

**Fixed: documents that carry junction-endpoint wires.** A branch whose `from`, or a feed wire whose `to`, **is** the junction. `findJunctionFeedWire` reads the structure outright there. Serialization permits the shape, `deserialize.ts` preserves it, and the legacy importer (#377) will read documents of it.

**Not fixed: documents the app writes today.** `completeJunctionWiring` copies the trunk's source into every branch it creates (`wiringActions.ts:859`, `const fromEndpoint = { ...originalWire.from }`) and is the only appender to `wireIds` (`:959`). So every wire a gesture-written junction lists has the same `from`, a destination pin on each `to`, and segments sharing the trunk's prefix up to the junction (`allSegments = [...sharedSegments, ...newSegments]`). `topologicalEval.ts:49` is false for all of them and `:50` falls back to the first **listed** wire in `state.wires` order — and every writer to `state.wires` pushes at the end or removes (`wireActions.ts:146/174`, four `filter` rebuilds, `deserialize.ts:204`), so that order is creation order, the same wire `wireIds[0]` named. **The positional read moved arrays; it did not go away.** The repo already records the premise at `topologicalEval.test.ts:1069-1073`.

Measured at `2f52456` (merge base) and `e2f6f87`, branches given the gesture's `from`, everything else identical to this PR's own reproduction:

```
wireIds     : [branch1, branch2, TRUNK']
state.wires : [branch1, branch2, TRUNK']
main   (wireIds.slice(1))      → survivors [branch1]   — TRUNK' and branch2 deleted
this PR (findJunctionFeedWire) → survivors [branch1]   — TRUNK' and branch2 deleted, no change
```

Found by this PR's verifier; reproduced independently twice while scoping. It is now **pinned in the repo** as `gesture-shaped branches: two user-drawn wires are still lost (known limit, #403)` — run it rather than trusting this table.

## Why this is scoped rather than extended (the option not taken)

The BLOCK offered a second route: give the rule something it can discriminate on. I looked for one and there isn't one in the document.

- **Endpoints don't discriminate.** Trunk and branch share one `from`; both `to` a destination pin.
- **Geometry doesn't either.** A branch's segments are the trunk's prefix plus its own tail, so the branch passes *through* the junction exactly as the trunk does, and turns there.
- **A stored `junction.trunkWireId` is the only honest signal, and it does not reach this case.** `placeJunctionOnWire` knows the trunk exactly (`junctionPlacementActions.ts:228`), but `removeWire` on the trunk is precisely what invalidates the record — and that is the reproduction. After it, promoting the re-drawn wire is a policy choice, not something the document states. Measured: in every *other* gesture-shaped case a recorded trunk gives the same answer as the rule already does, because `placeJunctionOnWire` always records the oldest wire and `state.wires` is creation-ordered. So the field would buy no measurable change here, while adding a persisted field, a migration and a deserialization default to a document model ADR-0020 §6/§7.5b **deletes** (junctions stop being domain entities; fan-out becomes a net's sinks list) and whose v1 corpus #376 still wants captured untouched.

**The defect that remains is also not the one #364 describes.** In a gesture-written document every listed wire is complete — two real endpoints, full segments — so `removeJunction` deleting all but one loses valid connections *whichever* one it keeps. Fixing that changes `removeJunction`'s contract and contradicts four pre-existing tests, so it is #403 with its own acceptance criteria, not a patch here. And nobody asks for it: `removeJunction` has **no UI caller** — its in-app path is `junctionUtils.ts:126` `applyJunctionRelocations`, reached by dragging a gate or a node (#395).

## Corrections made in this PR

- **`docs/development/observed-bugs.md` B-009 was wrong and is fixed.** It read *Status: Fixed* / *"Measured end to end through the real actions"* and sat under **Resolved**. Both were false for the documents the app writes. It is back under **Open** as **Partly fixed**, with separate *Fixed for* / *NOT fixed for* rows, the measurement, the reachability path, and the correction dated and owned. The #376 criterion — *capture the corpus before exercising `removeJunction`* — now stands for **every** document, not only ones saved before this fix.
- **The under-labelled fixtures are labelled, and the consequence is drawn.** `setWireIds` (no store action overwrites `wireIds`; every real writer is order-preserving) and the `to: junction` wire are both named now, and a SCOPE block at the head of the `describe` says plainly that these tests describe **the importer's world, not the app's**, and that the hand-written endpoints are load-bearing for every assertion that turns on telling a trunk from a branch.
- **The code says the limit too** — at `findJunctionFeedWire`'s definition and at `removeJunction`'s call site — so the next reader meets it before building on the rule.
- **A note is on #395**, whose suggested fix reuses `findJunctionFeedWire` and inherits the same hole.

## The verifier's nit 1 (the rule's home) — measured, and declined

`src/core/document/junctions.ts` is the better home on the merits, and the ratchet forbids it. The rule operates on `JunctionNode` / `CircuitDocument`, which live in `src/store/types.ts`, so:

```
src/core/document/junctions.ts   -> src/store/types.ts             NEW engine-no-state   (1 new, red)
src/simulation/topologicalEval.ts -> src/store/documentJunctions.ts NEW engine-no-state   (1 new, red)
```

Both measured with `pnpm run lint:layers` in this worktree. Where it is now is the only 0-new home (`simulationActions.ts:2` is the precedent). The real fix is to move the document types below both layers — ADR-0020 / #318 work. That reasoning is recorded at the import site so it is not re-litigated.

## Tests

`src/store/actions/signalActions/signalActions.test.ts`. The behaviour change was TDD'd at `177e31c` (test-only, fails 5 / passes 19 at that commit — checked by the verifier). This round adds no behaviour change; the two new tests were still written red-first: the gesture case was written asserting `[trunk2.id]` (the outcome #364 aims for), run, observed failing, and only then pinned to what actually happens with the `#403` marker on it.

- keeps the trunk when `wireIds[0]` genuinely is the trunk
- keeps the trunk when `wireIds[0]` is a branch
- keeps a feed wire that **ends** at the junction and is listed last
- keeps the feed wire of a junction fed from another junction (a chain)
- removes every listed wire when the junction has no feed wire
- keeps the trunk after it is deleted and re-drawn
- **gesture-shaped branches: two user-drawn wires are still lost (known limit, #403)** — the reproduction, pinned
- **gesture-shaped branches: an undisturbed fan-out still keeps its trunk** — the case #403 must not regress

No existing assertion weakened; the four pre-existing `removeJunction` tests pass untouched.

**Follow-ups:** #403 (the remaining data loss, with the measurement), #395 (`computeJunctionRelocations`, noted as inheriting the hole), and the verifier's nit 3 — a surviving feed wire that *ends* at the junction keeps a `to` pointing at the deleted junction, pre-existing and unchanged.

| `pnpm run test:run` | exit 0 — 138 files, **2206 tests passed**, 0 failed |
| `pnpm run build` | exit 0 — 2515 modules, built in 14.05s |

| Project-1 vectors (`project01.test.ts`, `core/testing/engine.test.ts`, `appRegistry.test.ts`) | exit 0 — 87 passed |

`main` moved to `f306a50` during this round (two HDL-compiler commits); they touch no file this PR touches, and the branch keeps `177e31c` / `e2f6f87` unrewritten so the verdict's SHAs stay reachable.
